subject: OPERATOR REVIEW: scraper snapshot found inside .git (possible past exposure)
description:
Found during marathon 2026-07-09: ~250 index.html directory-listing snapshots dated Jan 8 were sitting INSIDE .git/ (every objects/ fan-out dir, logs/, hooks/, etc.), titled 'Directory listing for /Ai content creation/Hexworth Prime/.git/...' — i.e. some HTTP server once served the repo's OLD location with directory listings on, and a crawler saved its own output back into the tree, including the full .git internals. All archived to _archive/git-stray-2026-07-09/ (we-do-not-destroy); git fsck clean afterward. WHY IT MATTERS: if that server was ever reachable by others, the entire git history (and any secrets in it) was browsable. Operator should decide: (a) identify what served that path in January (python http.server? node serve?), (b) whether exposure was local-only, (c) whether any secrets in repo history warrant rotation. Marathon continued; no action taken beyond archiving.
[2026-07-24 06:04] SECURITY ASSESSMENT 2026-07-24 (sub-question c — the load-bearing one — RESOLVED clean). Scanned tracked tree for real secrets: (1) private-key blocks (BEGIN RSA/OPENSSH/EC PRIVATE) in non-lab files: ZERO; (2) .env / serviceAccount*.json ever committed (--diff-filter=A all history): ZERO; (3) AWS/Slack/Stripe/GitHub live-token patterns: the ONLY AKIA hits are AWS's OWN published example key 'AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE' + synthetic teaching variants (AKIA...NOVA123/INITIAL), all inside dark-arts/bug-hunting + ehe LAB content (intentional, not real creds); (4) Firebase apiKey AIzaSyC3tWNETi... is the PUBLIC web-config key (public by Firebase design — security is Firestore rules + App Check, not key secrecy; expected in client bundles). CONCLUSION: even in the worst case (the Jan .git directory-listing WAS publicly reachable), there is NOTHING in history that warrants rotation — no real secret was ever committed. Sub-questions (a) what served the path in January and (b) local-only-vs-reachable remain forensically unknowable from here, but they are now LOW-STAKES given (c) is clean. Recommend: close as assessed-no-rotation-needed; (a)/(b) optional forensic curiosity. Firebase posture (App Check/rules enforcement) is a separate standing concern, not this exposure.
[2026-07-31 22:23] RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-31 against 279 commits landed since the 2026-07-24 assessment. Sub-question (c) -- the load-bearing one -- still CLEAN, and re-derived rather than trusted: (1) .env / serviceAccount*.json / credentials.json ever ADDED across ALL history: ZERO. (2) Private-key blocks: 23 files match, ALL decoy/simulated. Verified with a corrected detector -- my first metric measured the LONGEST base64 run, which cannot distinguish a decoy from a real PEM because real keys wrap at exactly 64 chars too. Counting CONSECUTIVE base64 chunks inside each BEGIN..END block instead: a real 2048-bit key body is ~25+ chunks; NO block in the repo has >=10. The 3 firmware .bin hits are a PEM parser's embedded format-string constants (BEGIN immediately followed by END, no body), i.e. mbedTLS/OpenSSL literals, not an embedded key. (3) NEW since the last assessment and worth recording: functions/quiz_keys.json now holds 619 answer keys. NOT web-reachable -- firebase.json public dir is _app, functions/ deploys to Cloud Functions; /quiz_keys.json, /functions/quiz_keys.json and a traversal attempt all return 404 on production, measured. CONCLUSION UNCHANGED: even in the worst case (the Jan .git listing was publicly reachable), nothing in history warrants rotation. Sub-questions (a) what served the path and (b) local-only-vs-reachable remain forensically unknowable and are LOW-STAKES given (c). Recommend closing as assessed-no-rotation-needed; this is an OPERATOR decision to close, so leaving it open.
